home.title: Trimly | Memories within Reach
home.description: Trimly finds the moments worth keeping in long recordings, cuts them out, and saves them back to Photos on the day and in the place they happened.

hero.eyebrow: A highlight editor for long recordings
hero.lede: Your best moments are buried in hour-long recordings. Trimly helps you find them, cut them out, and put them back in Photos, on the day and in the place they happened.

rolling.label: Keep rolling
rolling.copy: By the time you reach for the camera, the moment is already half over, so the best ones are the ones you missed. With Trimly you start recording when you arrive and stop when you leave. Keeping only the good parts takes minutes, not an evening.
rolling.afterSub: Record it all, keep the best

Drag in and out points, step frame by frame, follow the waveform. Make as many clips as you like, grab a still or a Live Photo, and give each one a label.

find.h2:
An hour of footage.
The good parts, found.
find.copy: On-device intelligence listens and looks through the recording for you: what was said, a laugh, an animal, words on screen, the beat of the music. You pick what to keep.

photos.h2: It lands on the day it happened.
photos.copy: Most editors save a clip as if it were shot today. Trimly works out the real moment of every frame, so each clip shows up next to the photos from that afternoon, with its place, camera and lens.

photos.trimlyDesc: Same clip sits under Wednesday, Oct 1, 2025 · 14:21, among that day’s photos. Info panel: map pin in the Serengeti, iPhone 17 Pro, Telephoto 100 mm ƒ2.8.

With Trimly you pick a LUT once and the graded look is saved straight back to the video in Photos. Scroll your library and it already looks like the day you had.

support.title: Trimly | Support
support.description: Answers to common questions about Trimly, and how to contact us.
support.lede: Answers to the questions people ask most. If yours isn’t here, write to us.
support.contactBody: Send feedback from Settings in Trimly: it attaches the app’s log, which helps us see what happened. Or email us directly.

items.q: Which devices does Trimly work on?
items.a: iPhone and iPad with iOS 18 or later, Mac with macOS 15 or later, and Apple TV with tvOS 18 or later. One purchase covers all of them.

items.q: Is there a subscription?
items.a: No. Trimly is a one-time purchase on the App Store.

items.q: Do I need an account?
items.a: No. There is no sign-in. If you use iCloud, your edits sync through your own iCloud account.

items.q: Where can I open videos from?
items.a: Your Photos library, the Files app, external drives, and network shares over SMB or WebDAV. You can also share a video to Trimly from another app, or drag files onto Trimly on Mac and iPad.

items.q: Does Trimly make a copy of my video?
items.a:
No. Trimly reads the original where it already is, so a long recording never takes up space twice.

The one exception is a video shared to Trimly from another app on iPhone or iPad. That one is copied, and you can review and delete those copies in Settings ▸ Imported Copies.

items.q: Which formats can Trimly open?
items.a: Most video and audio files your Apple device can play, such as MOV and MP4 video and common audio formats. Trimly also opens raw PCM recordings; it asks you for the sample format when you open one.

items.q: Why is a video from Photos slow to open?
items.a: If the original is stored in iCloud, it has to download first; you can cancel the download at any time. Videos you have edited in Photos can also take a little longer, because Photos prepares the edited version before Trimly can read it.

items.q: Can I cut several clips from one video?
items.a: Yes, as many as you like. Give each clip a label, and capture stills or Live Photos at any frame.

items.q: Can Trimly find the good parts for me?
items.a: Find Clips searches the recording on your device: what was said, sounds such as laughter or music, people and animals, text on screen, highlights, and the beat of the music. GoPro HiLight and DJI highlight marks appear too. You look through what it found and choose what to keep.

items.q: Why do my clips show up on the right day in Photos?
items.a: Trimly works out when each clip was really filmed from the original’s capture time, and saves it with that time, along with the location, camera and lens details when the original has them.

items.q: My travel clips show the wrong time. What can I do?
items.a: Set a time zone shift in Settings, and exported clips are saved with the local time where you filmed. If the camera’s own clock was wrong, set the correct capture time for that file, and every clip from it is corrected.

items.q: Does exporting reduce quality?
items.a: With transcoding set to Off, Trimly keeps the original picture and sound, and export is almost instant. A LUT, a crop or some rotations need the video to be re-encoded; choose Quality, Balance or Efficiency to trade quality against file size.

items.q: Can I take my selects into Final Cut Pro or another editor?
items.a: Yes. Export FCPXML or EDL for your editor, and SRT for subtitles.

items.q: Which LUTs are built in?
items.a: Rec. 709 conversions for Apple Log 2, DJI D-Log and D-Log M, GoPro GP-Log and Insta360 I-Log. You can also import your own .cube files, and they sync to your other devices through iCloud.

items.q: How do I see my graded Log footage in Photos?
items.a: Open the video from Photos and choose a LUT. With Settings ▸ Save LUT to Photos turned on (it is by default), Trimly saves the graded look to that video in Photos. The original Log is kept.

items.q: How do I remove the look again?
items.a: Choose No LUT for that video in Trimly. On a Mac you can also use Revert to Original in Photos.

items.q: Can I grade many videos at once?
items.a: Select several videos on Trimly’s home screen and apply a LUT to all of them. To grade a whole album, use the Save LUT to Photos action in Shortcuts.

items.q: Can I apply a LUT inside the Photos app?
items.a: Yes. On iPhone, iPad and Mac, Trimly adds a Photos editing extension that applies a LUT to a video right in Photos, for videos Photos lets you edit. For Log footage, use Save LUT to Photos instead.

items.q: What does iCloud sync?
items.a: Your clips, labels and other edits, and your LUT library. The videos themselves are never uploaded.

items.q: Can I start on one device and finish on another?
items.a: Yes. Your edits sync through iCloud, and Handoff lets you carry on from the next device. If the other device can reach the same file, through Photos, iCloud Drive or the same NAS, it opens where you left off.

items.q: Is my footage analysed in the cloud?
items.a: No. Find Clips and every other analysis runs on your device using Apple’s built-in frameworks. See the Privacy Policy.

items.q: Can I edit videos stored on my NAS?
items.a: Yes, over SMB or WebDAV. Trimly plays and cuts straight from the share, without downloading the whole file first.

items.q: Where are my NAS passwords stored?
items.a: In your device’s Keychain.

privacyPage.title: Trimly | Privacy Policy
privacyPage.description: Trimly collects no data. Your footage stays on your device.
privacyPage.intro: Trimly processes your media entirely on your device, and your footage stays on your iPhone, iPad, Mac or Apple TV. Edits and LUTs can sync across your Apple devices through iCloud, but video files are never uploaded. This policy explains, in plain terms, what that means for your privacy.

sections.p: Trimly does not collect, store, or transmit any personal information. There is no analytics, no tracking, no advertising identifiers, and no telemetry of any kind.

Trimly has no servers of its own, and it does not connect to any third-party service. The only network activity is iCloud sync: when you turn it on, Apple’s iCloud keeps your edits and LUTs in sync across your devices, under Apple’s iCloud terms and privacy policy. Video and audio files are never uploaded or synced.

When you open media from the Files app, external storage, a network share, or your Photos library, Trimly reads it only so you can trim and export it. All processing happens on your device, and exported clips are saved where you choose. Trimly accesses your Photos library only with your permission: to open the media you select, to save the clips you export, and, when you ask it to, to save a LUT look to a video in your library.
When you add an SMB or WebDAV share, Trimly connects only to the address you enter. The password is stored in your device’s Keychain.

sections.h: No account, no third-party network access
sections.p: Trimly has no account system and no sign-in. Apart from Apple’s built-in iCloud sync and the network shares you add, it makes no network connections, and it does not use any analytics service or cloud processing.

All of Trimly’s AI features run on frameworks built into Apple’s systems. Trimly doesn’t include any third-party AI models, and never will. It doesn’t share your data with any third-party AI provider. Everything runs locally on your device, under the same privacy rules that apply to AI features across Apple’s systems.
Because Trimly collects no data at all, it does not knowingly collect information from anyone, including children.
If this policy changes, the updated version will be posted on this page with a new date.
